messages.subject: How SPDE+FEA uses data
parts:
Hello, 

I read this paper about approximating a Gaussian process using SPDE and FEA but I couldn't understand where the data are used to fit the model! All I understood is that if we want to fit a Gaussian process with Matern covariance function to our spatial data we can assume that the solution can be found by solving a specific SPDE which itself requires numerical methods like finite elements to solve. My question is where the data comes into play? Are we using data to define the SPDE and then solve it using FEA? If yes how do we define the SPDE using data and if not then how exactly our goal which is finding the Gaussian process from which our data/observations are generated is satisfied? 

Best,
Amin

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How SPDE+FEA uses data
parts:
Hi Amin,

the finite element method is used to construct the prior distribution of the weights for the basis functions, which would work the same also for other basis function choices; the observations are linked to the basis functions at each observation location, which defines the joint distribution of the field and the observations, and from there the posterior distribution of the basis weights is estimated; for additive Gaussian observation noise, this involves a straightforward conditional Gaussian distribution construction. See for example the (brief) section 1.2 in the https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v063i19 paper, and slide 40 of these lecture slides: https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~flindgre/cuso2019/cuso2019.pdf

In other words, we rarely "solve" the spde associated with the problem; we only use it construct the needed distributions.

Finn
